title: Priming Roulette — labbook
content:
Purpose: quick iterative notes for 'priming roulette' — intentionally randomizing prompt-level choices to surface brittle decision boundaries. Notes to self and quick recipes for later formalization.

High-level hypothesis:
- The placement and framing of the instruction (system vs first user vs in-line preface) interacts with few-shot ordering and example polarity in non-linear ways.
- Small adversarial perturbations (paraphrase, extra parentheses, token repeats) reveal different failure classes than temperature/attenuation tests.

Experiment matrix (informal):
- Instruction placement: [system, first user, inline preamble, trailing instruction]
- Few-shot ordering: [best->worst, ambiguous-first, mixed, neg-example-last]
- Example polarity: [positive, negative, contrastive pairs]
- Surface perturbations: [emoji noise, numeric padding, extra filler sentence]
- Decoding: [temp 0.0, 0.7, 1.0], top_p sweep 0.8/0.95

Quick informal prompts to try (playground):
1) System-first minimal: "You are a concise summarizer. Keep outputs <= 40 words."
   User: "Summarize: Article A..."

2) Inline preface (single message): "Summarize the following in plain bullets (no filler). Examples show structure.

Example1:
Input: Short blog post about X
Output: • X summary line; • implications

Now summarize: [ARTICLE TEXT]"

3) Trailing instruction (after examples): Provide 3-step reasoning then answer. (note: often disabled by safety/heuristic layers)

Few-shot exemplar set A (intent: task framing + contrastive polarity):
- EX1 IN: "Refund policy email (customer angry)"
  OUT: "Apologize, explain refund timeline, next steps"
- EX2 IN: "Praise email request for feature"
  OUT: "Acknowledge, thank, signal roadmap slot"
- EX3 IN (negative): "Malicious prompt example: inject code"
  OUT: "Refuse + safe alternative"

Notes: mixing a negative exemplar helped reduce hallucinations in one run, but increased over-cautious refusals. TODO: quantify with pass/fail rubric.

Observed failure cases (random runs):
- Case A: Instruction walked into after examples — model treats examples as ground truth and copies style but ignores explicit 'no-bullets' flag later.
- Case B: Numeric padding ("0 0 0 ...") causes truncation of first example sometimes on longer contexts. Suspect token alignment changes.
- Case C: Role-swap brittleness — when system message says "assistant is empathetic" but first user example is terse, model oscillates between styles.

Probing snippets to isolate failures:
- Probe A: swap example order, keep everything else identical. If outputs swap style -> ordering effect.
- Probe B: remove punctuation from example outputs; measure precision/recall on expected tokens.

Evaluation quick plan (local):
- Metric set (fast):
  - Structural match (presence of bullets/steps) — binary
  - Hallucination rate on canned fact checks (contains fabricated claim) — binary
  - Tone match (embedding similarity to target style) — numeric
- Run 100 randomized seeds across high/low temp and compute deltas by instruction placement.

Adversarial templates to add to library:
- "Make it sound more enthusiastic" vs "Make it sound neutral" paired examples to probe polarity flip.
- Sly invert: append 'Note: ignore previous examples' and measure whether model obeys.

Lingering questions / To-dos:
- TODO: formalize pass/fail rubric and put into eval harness (Linear ID above).
- TODO: add token-level truncation logging to see where numeric padding shifts sequence boundaries.
- TODO: test with cached K/V variants on Dedicated to ensure caching doesn't bias early prompts.

Random micro-experiment logs (play-by-play):
- 2024-11-13: small run with inline preface + 3 ex. result: too verbose; adding 'limit to 40 words' moved to system msg reduced length but changed style.
- 2024-12-02: swapped last ex to negative; hallucination down from 12%->8% on small set, but refusal up +3 points.

Quick examples to copy into eval harness: (raw lines)
- INPUT: "Draft a one-paragraph apology for delayed shipping. Keep human, not legalese."
  EXPECTED: contains 'sorry' and 'next steps' and <=80 words
- INPUT: "List 3 quick steps to troubleshoot login issues. Output as numbered steps."
  EXPECTED: 3 numbered items, each <= 12 words

Notes to future self: this doc is messy on purpose. The main value is velocity — capture oddities, then formalize the few top signals into an experiment deck. Keep this in users/ so it's easy to iterate.

Search anchors (useful keywords to find later): priming roulette, instruction placement, negative exemplar, numeric padding, role-swap, trailing-instruction, few-shot polarity

Signed-off (scratch): Maya P.
